subject: Myth & Symbolism
subcategory: The World Tree and Cosmic Maps
title: The Totem Pole

hook.text: Pacific Northwest totem poles stack animal and ancestor figures vertically—a carved axis linking families to the cosmos.

buildup.text: Each figure on the pole tells a story: raven, eagle, bear, whale. The pole is a vertical narrative.

discovery.text: Totem poles aren't worshipped. They're read. Each one records history, clan rights, and mythic events.

twist.text: Colonizers misread totem poles as idols. They're actually closer to heraldry—coats of arms carved in wood.

climax.text: The totem pole is an axis mundi that tells a specific community's story. The center of the world is personal.

punchline.text: Read it bottom to top. That's your history.

quiz.question: What function do totem poles primarily serve?
options: Recording history, clan rights, and mythic events
